insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited

great.name: Restore/Additional SI buffer: ReAssure (unlimited, after 1st paid claim)
great.quote: The first paid claim triggers ReAssure, a benefit with unlimited sum insured.
great.explanation: Acts like an additional sum insured once your first claim is paid, helping cover future claims even after base SI is used (note: per-claim payout from ReAssure is capped at up to Base Sum Insured).

great.name: Restore benefit covers subsequent claims including same illness (because ReAssure is not limited to unrelated illnesses in wording)
great.quote: The first paid claim triggers ReAssure, a benefit with unlimited sum insured.
great.explanation: This is stronger than standard ‘restore’ because it provides an additional pool after the first paid claim, without restricting it only to unrelated illnesses in the provided text.

good.name: PED waiting period: 24 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 2 years of continuous coverage, which is standard.

good.name: Specific illness/procedure waiting period: 24 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.
good.reference: Section 5.1(II) Specified disease/procedure waiting period (Code- Excl02)
good.explanation: The listed specific diseases are covered after 24 months; this is standard in the market.

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident
good.explanation: 30-day initial waiting is standard (accidents covered immediately).

good.name: Pre-hospitalization: 60 days
good.quote: We will pay expenses incurred on consultations, medicines, diagnostic tests 60 days before date of admission
good.reference: Section 3.3 Expenses before and after hospitalization (Pre & Post hospitalization)
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for 60 days before admission (standard/good).

good.name: Post-hospitalization: 180 days
good.quote: and 180 days after date of discharge
good.reference: Section 3.3 Expenses before and after hospitalization (Pre & Post hospitalization)
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses up to 180 days after discharge (upper end of standard).

good.name: NCB/Renewal bonus: 10% per claim-free year up to 100% (but claim impact not specified here)
good.quote: For every claim free year, we will add 10% of expiring policy base sum insured as NCB, maximum up to 100%.
good.explanation: Sum Insured can increase with claim-free renewals (10% per year up to 100%). Whether it reduces/resets on a claim is not stated in the excerpt.

bad.name: Room rent: Not stated in provided text (assumed not covered/available from document) — verify Policy Schedule
bad.quote: All applicable benefits and details are mentioned in your Policy Schedule.
bad.explanation: Room rent eligibility (e.g., Any Room / Single AC / capping) is not provided here. Since it’s a core cost driver, treat as a gap and confirm from Policy Schedule.

bad.name: Mandatory co-pay is very high by default (50% on admissible claim amount)
bad.quote: The default co-payment in the product is 50% which You can modify to 40% or 30% or 20% at inception of the first policy.
bad.explanation: A 50% co-pay means you pay half of every admissible claim by default. Even if you can choose a lower co-pay at inception, this is still a major reduction in effective coverage.

bad.name: Extra 10% co-pay if hospitalized in higher room category than eligible
bad.quote: You will have to bear additional 10% co-payment IF treatment is taken in higher room category than the eligible room category as specified in Your Policy Schedule
bad.explanation: If you choose a room above eligibility, you bear an additional 10% co-pay, increasing out-of-pocket.

bad.name: Consumables not covered (out-of-pocket for items like gloves, masks, kits, etc.)
bad.quote:
Annexure I – The expenses that are not covered or subsumed into room charges / procedure charges / costs of treatment
List  I – Expenses not covered ... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 57 NEBULISATION KIT ... 58 ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED
bad.reference: Annexure I – List I (Expenses not covered)
bad.explanation: Many common consumables and hospital items are listed as not covered, which can materially increase hospital bills paid by you.

bad.name: Modern treatment sub-limit: Robotic surgeries capped at ₹1,00,000 per claim (with exceptions)
bad.quote: NOTE: A limit of maximum Rs. 1,00,000 per claim will apply to all robotic surgeries, except for total radical prostatectomy, cardiac surgeries, partial nephrectomy and surgeries for malignancies.
bad.explanation: A sub-limit on robotic surgeries can be restrictive because robotic procedures often cost significantly more than ₹1,00,000.

unclear.name: Co-pay terms after inception (whether 20/30/40/50% selected; and whether any 0% option exists)
unclear.quote: The default co-payment in the product is 50% which You can modify to 40% or 30% or 20% at inception of the first policy.
unclear.explanation: The actual co-pay applicable to you depends on what was chosen at inception (and it cannot be changed later). Confirm your selected co-pay in the Policy Schedule.

unclear.name: NCB behavior on claim (reset/reduction) not stated in provided text
unclear.quote: For every claim free year, we will add 10% of expiring policy base sum insured as NCB, maximum up to 100%.
unclear.explanation: It states how NCB accrues, but does not specify what happens to accumulated NCB after a claim (reduce/reset/fully protected). Confirm from full wording/schedule.

unclear.name: Cashless network size not specified
unclear.quote: Cashless claim facility is available at our network hospitals ONLY. As list of network hospitals is dynamic, for the latest list, refer to our website www.nivabupa.com.
unclear.explanation: The number of network hospitals is not mentioned here; network size impacts ease of cashless hospitalization.
